rejected.title: Ordering integers on a number line
card: Integers are whole numbers that can be negative, zero or positive. Examples are −7, 0 and 12. Fractions and decimals are not integers.
On a number line, zero sits in the middle. Positive integers are to the right and negative integers are to the left.
Numbers further to the right are larger. So 2 is greater than −5, and −2 is greater than −5 because −2 is further right.
With negatives, the number that looks bigger is smaller. −9 is less than −3, as −9 is further left. To order from least to greatest, go from left to right.
rejected.remember: Further right is larger. Further left is smaller.

a.q: Which list shows the integers in order from least to greatest?
a.why: Least to greatest goes from left to right on the number line, so −6 comes first, then −1, 0 and 4. The list −1, −6, 0, 4 is tempting, but −6 is further left than −1, so it is smaller.
a.clue: Picture the number line and read from left to right.

b.q: At 5 am on a winter morning, the temperatures were: Alice Springs −3°C, Thredbo −8°C, Hobart 2°C, Canberra −5°C. Which place was the coldest?
b.why: The coldest place has the least temperature, which is the number furthest left on the number line. −8 is further left than −5, −3 and 2, so Thredbo was the coldest. Canberra is tempting because −5 is also a negative temperature, but −8 is further left, so it is smaller.
b.clue: The coldest is the number furthest to the left.

b.q: At 5 am, the temperatures in four towns were: Alice Springs −3°C, Hobart −8°C, Perth 2°C, Canberra −5°C. Which town was the coldest?
b.why: The coldest town has the least temperature, which is the number furthest left on the number line. −8 is further left than −5 and −3, so Hobart was the coldest. Canberra is tempting because it is a lower number than Hobart's when you ignore the signs, but −5 is greater than −8.
b.clue: The coldest is the number furthest to the left.

problems.detail: Hobart at −8°C is unrealistic. Hobart's record low is about −2.8°C. Alice Springs and Canberra are known for colder winter mornings, so the example could mislead students, especially in Tasmania. Use plausible temperatures or swap the towns.

The why's reasoning for the Canberra distractor is confused. A student who ignores the signs and looks for the lowest number would pick Perth (2), not Canberra (5). The explanation needs rewording, for example: Canberra is tempting because −5 is one of the negative temperatures, but −8 is further left.
